twin.0x0: Stored 0 (no change); PLL3RDY 0.

differs: For 1: PLL3RDY is 1 on the first read after the write, with no lock time; silicon sets it when PLL3 locks (p383, p347-348).
observable_by_firmware: Yes, by reading RCC_CR.PLL3RDY: the armed firmware reads CR at L226 straight after PLL1ON/PLL2ON/PLL3ON = 1 (L225) and gets 0x3F003025 (all three RDY set). If that read is a wait loop it exits at its first iteration in the twin and after the lock time on silicon: iteration count and timing change, the data after it do not. The kernel clocks taken from PLL3 (armed I2C123SEL = 01 and ADCSEL = 01, pll3_r_ck; RCC_D2CCIP2R 0xE01009 at L234, RCC_D3CCIPR 0x10010100 at L236) are also available at once.
notes: One rule for every ready flag here: the stock model computes xRDY as the ON bit (FieldMode.Read with valueProviderCallback: _ => xon.Value), so the flag is 1 on the first read after the ON write; RM0433 says the flag is set by hardware once the oscillator is stable or the PLL locked, and gives no duration (the start-up and lock times are in the datasheet). The row text's "only gates PLLSRC/HSIDIV changes" understates the guard: PLL3ON feeds PllOn (L1141-1144), Running (L1079-1084), TVI-RCC-PLL (L771, L781) and TVI-RCC-PLL-REF (L810-815). Its clear while a running peripheral uses its output is TVI-RCC-CLOCK's; not exercised (no CR write after the PLLs start). PLL hardware clear on Stop/Standby (p383) is not modeled; no run writes SCR (nvic offset 0xD10, where SLEEPDEEP is; nvic writes are logged, e.g. VTOR at 0xD08) and PWR_CPUCR is written 0x0 only (armed L195, ap-fx), so no run enters Stop or Standby.
from_memory: That the read at L226 is a wait loop on PLLxRDY (ChibiOS hal_lld): the log shows one read, not the code.
That Stop and Standby need SCR.SLEEPDEEP = 1 and that SCR resets to 0 (ARMv7-M), so with SCR never written SLEEPDEEP stays 0.
